videos.title: Tomoyuki Yamashita's 3 Greatest Moves | The Tiger of Malaya and the Trial That Hanged Him
videos.desc:
On the eighth of December 1941, an hour before the bombs fell on Pearl Harbor, Japanese troops waded ashore at Kota Bharu in northern Malaya. By the middle of February the fortress of Singapore had surrendered. The general behind it was Tomoyuki Yamashita, an officer his own government had kept at a distance.

videos.title: Bernard Montgomery's 3 Greatest Moves | The Cautious General Who Beat Rommel
videos.desc:
At twenty to ten on the night of 23 October 1942, around nine hundred British guns opened fire along the Alamein line while the man who planned it slept in his caravan. Field Marshal Rommel was not even in Egypt. Ten weeks earlier, Bernard Montgomery had never commanded the Eighth Army.

Montgomery was born in London in 1887, the son of a clergyman who became Bishop of Tasmania. He was shot through the lung at Meteren in 1914, learned from the staff what unprepared attacks cost, and in August 1942 took over an army that expected to lose. videos.title: Erwin Rommel's 3 Greatest Moves | The Desert Fox Behind the Legend
videos.desc:
On the thirteenth of May 1940 German rubber boats were being shot to pieces on the river Meuse at Dinant. A German general came down to the bank, had the houses set on fire for smoke, and crossed in one of the boats himself. A week later his division was so far ahead that its own high command had lost track of it.

Erwin Rommel was born in Heidenheim in 1891, won the Pour le Merite in the Italian mountains in 1917, and in 1940 got the 7th Panzer Division without ever having commanded tanks. Two years later he was a field marshal, and the most famous German general of the war.

videos.title: Richard O'Connor's 3 Greatest Moves | The Forgotten General Who Won Britain's First Victory
videos.desc:
On the fifth of February 1941 a small British column came out of the Libyan desert and blocked the coast road at Beda Fomm. Thirty minutes later the head of the whole Italian Tenth Army came down that road. Two days later it surrendered. The general who planned it was a small, quiet man who hated publicity, and two months later he was a prisoner of the Germans because his driver took a wrong turn in the dark.

videos.title: Hasso von Manteuffel's 3 Greatest Moves | The Little General of the Bulge
videos.desc:
On Christmas Eve 1944 the tanks of the 2nd Panzer Division stood in the snow a few kilometres from the river Meuse, further west than any German unit in the Battle of the Bulge. videos.title: Walter Model's 3 Greatest Defensive Moves | Hitler's Fireman
videos.desc:
In April 1945 Field Marshal Walter Model was trapped in the Ruhr with more than three hundred thousand men. He would not surrender and he would not order a last stand. He dissolved his army, sent the old men and the boys home, and walked into a wood near Duisburg.

For three years he had been the man Hitler sent whenever a front was about to collapse.
